method_summary: Under dd-selfproto-v1.3 with trainer-supplied official DD EMA initialization and frozen training/evaluation settings, prepare 128 teacher targets from three proposals per original label using stable lower-median LPIPS-distance selection. Use teacher_steps=10, guidance=2.0, top_k=900, top_p=0.95, ode_nfe=32, logSNR grid, one pass and uniform weights. Adjacent sampled times pair one U[0,0.1) anchor with one antithetic U[0.1,1] context in random orientation; tensors and random draws stay on CPU.
causal_hypothesis: Unvalidated hypothesis: selecting the median of three teacher/student LPIPS distances may balance target consistency and variation, while pairing an inference-near time anchor with a broader context time may improve low-time learning without losing coverage. Any FID benefit remains unmeasured; CPU interface PASS provides no quality or score evidence.
next_step_decision_rule: Wait for a later trusted, complete public FID evaluation tied to the verified source SHA and dd-selfproto-v1.3 protocol. Only then record the actual finite FID and compare it with a trusted best evaluated under the same protocol; retain this candidate only if its FID is strictly lower, or establish the first evaluated reference if no trusted best exists. Ties or worse FID do not replace an existing best. Missing, partial, failed, untrusted or source-mismatched evaluations cannot support a score or a retention decision; CPU PASS is never QA or FID evidence. Until such evidence exists, keep PREPARED_NOT_EVALUATED, score=null and retained_best=false.
